Apprehending arrest in Crime No.1098/2022 of North Parur police station, registered for offences under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, accused 1 to 5 have filed this petition.

2. The prosecution allegation is that the petitioners, who are Managing Directors of the Company,
namely NFBI, have collected an amount of Rs.10,22,770/- from the defacto complainant with the intention of making an unlawful gain to the accused and unlawful loss to the complainant.
The allegation is that accused persons 1 to 5 owners of the firm NFBI headquartered in Kozhikode promised to pay Area Dealership at Paravur Constituency.

After receiving Rs.10,43,700/- in total till date, the area dealership along with the products, has not been delivered and also did not refund the amount paid by the complainant and thereby committing the aforementioned offences.
3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor were heard.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners argues that they are innocent of the allegations levelled against them.
They have been running the NFBI Business Service LLP for the past several years without any complaints from any quarter.
Accused Nos.1 to 3 are the Designated partners of the LLP, and accused No. 1 is handling the business operations mainly.

The other petitioners are Jayadeep vs State Of Kerala on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75633434/
2 employees of the enterprise.
Understanding the electric segment market in the economy, the petitioners herein launched NFBI shopping cart promoting electrical bicycles or e-bikes.
An e-bike is a notarized bicycle that comprises an integrated electric motor to assist propulsion.
The fact that they emit less pollution per kilometre than cars and bikes is why they are popular.
Riding an electric cycle is similar to riding a normal cycle but with the added benefit of an electric motor.
The petitioners were giving franchises all over Kerala promoting NFBI e-bikes, and one Sandhya Sreekanth approached the petitioners herein to start a franchise.
5. The defacto complainant and his wife applied for a Mudra loan.
The project was for starting an MSME.
The company named J Trade was the financial consultant.
The first petitioner herein is the Managing Director of the enterprise.
The petitioner's enterprise also provides loan assistance for starting the NFBI E SHOPPING CART, which has the required business place.
The same is mentioned in Annexure A2, dealership application.
The defacto complainant's wife applied for a business loan from the Bank of India, North Paravoor Branch, submitting the SME project for starting a firm styled M/s.SAAS NFBI E SHOPPING CART.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The bank after verifying the credentials of the petitioner's company, sanctioned the loan and credited the same to the NFBI Bank account.
The loan was sanctioned on 12.8.2022, and the amount credited was Rs.10,22,770/-.

Thereafter,
Sandhya Sreekanth executed a memorandum of understanding with the NFBI Business Services LLP on 15.8.2022.
6.
Learned counsel for the defacto complainant argues that Annexure A4 and Annexure A5 filed by the petitioners/respondents herein are forged documents.
The signatures seen in the copies marked as Annexures A4 and A5 are not signed by the third respondent and are not within the knowledge of these respondents.

The Mudra loan of Rs.10 lakh is sanctioned to the third respondent from BOI,
Paravur Branch and not from Indian Bank, Paravur Branch, as stated in Annexure A5.

The amount of Rs.1,00,000/- has been transferred to the ICICI North Paravur Branch account maintained by the additional second respondent as MSME subsidy promised by the petitioners at the time of dealership discussions, not as stated in Annexure A5. Annexure R1, wherein the additional third respondent (the defacto complainant) has not signed till this date due to the disagreement in the terms and conditions of the agreement.

The petitioners demanded the additional second and third respondents to collect Rs.2500/- each from 100 people, totalling Rs.2,50,000/- by issuing a slip, an illegal lottery-like business against the terms and conditions of the dealership agreement.

7. Learned Public Prosecutor opposing the bail application submitted that with an intention to cause unjust profit to the accused and unjust loss to the complainant, accused Nos. 1 to 3 of NFBI firm headquartered at Kozhikode started collecting money from the complainant by promising to provide area dealership in Paravur constituency.

Believing the words of the accused, the complainant started transferring money from 09.06.2022 to 12.08.2022 from his ICICI Bank, North Paravur Branch from account No. 105301500421 to the accused bank account No.626505500459.
On 9.6.2022, the complainant transferred Rs.3000/-.
On 14.6.2022 and 4.7.2022, he transferred Rs.10000/- and Rs.7930/- to the accused bank account No.922020008036099 through this Google Pay account on 12.08.2022.
The complainant transferred Rs.10,22,770/- from his account No.856420110000260 to the accused account No626505500459.

Altogether, Rs.10,43,700/- was transferred by the complainant to the accused till date without giving the area dealership or products and without Jayadeep vs State Of Kerala on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75633434/
3 returning the amount; all accused cheated the complainant by committing fraud.

sentences.text: 8. Having considered the rival contentions, it is to be noted that the defacto complainant had availed a Mudra loan, and the said amount was directly transferred to the account of the petitioners.
Notwithstanding the payment, it is the specific contention of the defacto complainant that the dealership or the vehicles are not given, disabling them from functioning.

It is also their argument that the agreements and documents produced on behalf of the petitioners are forged, and their signatures are forged, the agreement was not signed, and the document is produced as if there is a signed agreement between the parties when none of these things has happened.

On the face of the allegation of cheating and also having forged documents, there has to be a proper investigation as regards the role of each accused, whether there are other similar antecedents against the petitioners,
whether
the Mudra loan advanced by the complainant could have reached the account of the accused

. These are all matters where a proper investigation, including a custodial interrogation,
should be carried out, and the grant of anticipatory bail in such a case will certainly hamper a proper investigation.
Under such circumstances, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioners, and accordingly, the bail application is dismissed and the following direction issued.

In the event the petitioners surrender before the Investigating Officer in two weeks, they shall be interrogated and thereafter, shall be produced before the Magistrate having jurisdiction on the date of surrender itself.
If the petitioners move for bail, the court below shall, untrammelled by any of the observations in this order, consider the bail applications on merit as expeditiously as possible.
If the petitioners do not surrender before the Investigating Officer, as directed above, the Investigating Officer will be free to arrest the petitioners as if no order has been passed in this case.
Subject to the above, the bail application is dismissed.

Sd/-
MOHAMMED NIAS C.P. JUDGE dlk 16.11.2023 APPENDIX OF BAIL APPL.
